sentences.en: This is 99% Invisible.
sentences.zh: 这里是百分之九十九隐形。

sentences.en: I'm Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 我是罗曼·马尔斯。

sentences.en: Oop, that's my phone.
sentences.zh: 噢，那是我的手机。

sentences.en: Sorry, let me just dismiss that.
sentences.zh: 不好意思，我挂掉一下。

sentences.en: Producer James T.
sentences.zh: 制作人詹姆斯·T·

sentences.en: Green.
sentences.zh: 格林。

sentences.en: Sorry, honestly, it's just rare that I even keep my phone on vibrate or anything other than silent.
sentences.zh: 抱歉，说实话，我很少让手机保持震动或非静音状态。

sentences.en: It's kind of rare that I get calls at all.
sentences.zh: 我几乎很少接到电话。

sentences.en: Yeah, because millennials are killing phone calls.
sentences.zh: 对，因为千禧一代正在杀死电话。

sentences.en: I mean, well, kind of, but I can still remember a time Bridgewood phone calls.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，也算吧，但我还记得以前常打座机电话的时候。

sentences.en: Like, specifically when I was younger, probably around 15 years old.
sentences.zh: 比如，具体在我更年轻的时候，大概15岁左右。

sentences.en: I remember family parties at my great-grandmother's house.
sentences.zh: 我记得在我曾祖母家举行的家庭聚餐。

sentences.en: The smells were that of pound cake and baked macaroni and cheese.
sentences.zh: 空气中弥漫着磅蛋糕和烤通心粉加奶酪的味道。

sentences.en: The sounds were of gossip and complaints and bravado.
sentences.zh: 耳边充斥着八卦、抱怨和虚张声势。

sentences.en: But there's one noise that was constant, and it came from my uncle Scooter.
sentences.zh: 但有一种声音从未间断，它来自我的叔叔斯库特。

sentences.en: Or rather, from his phone.
sentences.zh: 或者更准确地说，来自他的手机。

sentences.en: See, family functions in my mother's house back then.
sentences.zh: 看吧，那时候在我妈妈家里的家庭聚会。

sentences.en: Everybody left their cell phones on, even before they blessed the food.
sentences.zh: 每个人都开着手机，甚至在餐前祷告之前。

sentences.en: See, Scooter was the definition of a cool uncle.
sentences.zh: 看吧，斯库特就是酷叔叔的代名词。

sentences.en: I remember him wearing a lot of white, even though our meals were pretty messy.
sentences.zh: 我记得他经常穿一身白，尽管我们的饭菜很容易弄脏衣服。

sentences.en: He was a sunglasses indoors kind of guy.
sentences.zh: 他是那种在室内戴太阳镜的人。

sentences.en: Sitting at the head of the table, as he leaned back, the sunlight through the screen door would shine on his link bracelet.
sentences.zh: 坐在桌子主位，当他往后靠时，穿过纱门的阳光会照在他的链式手链上。

sentences.en: And his flip phone was always clipped to his belt.
sentences.zh: 而且他的翻盖手机总是夹在皮带上。

sentences.en: Because Scooter got a lot of calls.
sentences.zh: 因为斯库特有很多电话要接。

sentences.en: It may have been rude of me, but I wanted to hear my phone.
sentences.zh: 我这么做可能有点粗鲁，但我当时真的很想听见我的手机响。

sentences.en: I wanted it to ring.
sentences.zh: 我希望它能响起来。

sentences.en: Scooter was always getting up from the table to go to the corner of the room and whisper on the phone.
sentences.zh: 斯库特总是从桌旁站起来，走到房间角落里对着电话低声细语。

sentences.en: Or step out on the porch.
sentences.zh: 或者走到门廊上去。

sentences.en: Sometimes, he'd take the call right there in front of everyone.
sentences.zh: 有时，他会当着所有人的面直接接听电话。

sentences.en: And we all remember the song his phone would play.
sentences.zh: 我们都记得他的手机会播放的那首歌。

sentences.en: It seared into my brain.
sentences.zh: 它深深烙印在我的脑海里。

sentences.en: My ringtone is this woman's work by Maxwell.
sentences.zh: 我的铃声是麦克斯韦的《这女人的工作》。

sentences.en: Uncle Scooter had a lot of girlfriends.
sentences.zh: 斯库特叔叔有很多女朋友。

sentences.en: And so, his phone, a hollow mono speaker blasting Maxwell's smooth neo-soul sound, rang all the time.
sentences.zh: 所以，他的手机——一个单声道空洞喇叭，播放着麦克斯韦流畅的新灵魂乐——总是在响。

sentences.en: It never went beyond the first few seconds.
sentences.zh: 它从来没超过前几秒钟。

sentences.en: So, you just hear the...
sentences.zh: 所以，你只能听到...

sentences.en: Before he flips open his clamshell phone.
sentences.zh: 在他掀开他的翻盖手机之前。

sentences.en: The song starts out, you know, he starts to scream, you know.
sentences.zh: 歌曲刚开始，你知道的，他开始尖叫，你知道的。

sentences.en: So, when this ringtone goes off around people, it grabs their attention.
sentences.zh: 所以，当这个铃声在人群中响起时，会吸引所有人的注意。

sentences.en: Especially, by me being a single man, it caught a lot of girls' eyes.
sentences.zh: 尤其是作为一个单身汉的我，它吸引了很多女孩的目光。

sentences.en: And their ears, too.
sentences.zh: 还有她们的耳朵。

sentences.en: And this is the time when everyone had ringtones.
sentences.zh: 这也是每个人都有手机铃声的时代。

sentences.en: When the song your phone played really said something about you.
sentences.zh: 手机播放的歌曲真的能说明你是怎样的人。

sentences.en: I never had a ringtone myself.
sentences.zh: 我自己从来没有设过铃声。

sentences.en: Maybe for the same reason I never got a tattoo.
sentences.zh: 也许原因跟我从不做纹身是一样的。

sentences.en: I never wanted to commit to something so personal and so public.
sentences.zh: 我从不想对如此私密又如此公开的事情做出承诺。

sentences.en: Yeah, ringtones were really meaningful.
sentences.zh: 对，铃声真的很有意义。

sentences.en: And they could be different for all of your friends.
sentences.zh: 而且你所有的朋友可以设置不同的铃声。

sentences.en: I remember I'd scroll through, like, my 15 contacts,
sentences.zh: 我记得我会滑动查看我那大约15个联系人，

sentences.en: figuring out what was the best ringtone to assign for folks in my phone.
sentences.zh: 琢磨着给手机里的每个人分配什么铃声最好。

sentences.en: Like, what song would play when my best friend calls.
sentences.zh: 比如，我最好的朋友打电话时会播放什么歌。

sentences.en: Or my mom.
sentences.zh: 或者我妈妈。

sentences.en: And my crush.
sentences.zh: 还有我暗恋的人。

sentences.en: That's a whole lot of Usher.
sentences.zh: 那里面有大量的亚瑟小子。

sentences.en: I mean, like, who wasn't listening to Usher at that time?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，当时谁不听亚瑟小子呢？

sentences.en: But it wasn't just Usher.
sentences.zh: 但可不止有亚瑟小子。

sentences.en: You could go vintage with a timeless track.
sentences.zh: 你可以选择一首永恒曲目的复古老歌。

sentences.en: Or you could grab a new single and change it up with the newest, hottest song.
sentences.zh: 或者你可以找一张新单曲，换上最新、最火的歌曲。

sentences.en: These little 15-second melodies were these disposable, yet highly personal trinkets.
sentences.zh: 这些短短15秒的旋律就像是那种用过即弃却又极具个人色彩的小玩意儿。

sentences.en: And it was all thanks to this guy.
sentences.zh: 这一切都要归功于这个人。

sentences.en: My name is Vesa Mattipanen, but everybody calls me Vesku.
sentences.zh: 我叫韦萨·马蒂帕宁，但大家都叫我韦斯库。

sentences.en: Vesku is the father of the custom ringtone, which was conceived at a party in Finland in 1997.
sentences.zh: 韦斯库是定制铃声之父，这个概念于1997年在芬兰的一场派对上诞生。

sentences.en: At that time, I was 27 years old.
sentences.zh: 当时我27岁。

sentences.en: And I was living in downtown Helsinki.
sentences.zh: 住在赫尔辛基市中心。

sentences.en: And Wednesday was really the night to go out, hang around with your friends.
sentences.zh: 周三真的是外出和朋友闲逛的绝佳夜晚。

sentences.en: And it was a gloomy November evening.
sentences.zh: 那是一个阴沉的十一月傍晚。

sentences.en: Finland was in the midst of its Nokia-inspired tech boom.
sentences.zh: 芬兰正处于诺基亚掀起的科技热潮之中。

sentences.en: And a lot of Vesku's drinking buddies worked in tech.
sentences.zh: 韦斯库的很多酒肉朋友都在科技行业工作。

sentences.en: And during these discussions, everybody was having their phones with them.
sentences.zh: 在这些讨论中，每个人都随身带着手机。

sentences.en: What is the coolest phone?
sentences.zh: 哪款手机最酷？

sentences.en: And showing the new stuff that you can do with that.
sentences.zh: 然后展示用它能做的新鲜玩意儿。

sentences.en: You were, like, sitting around the table showing off.
sentences.zh: 你们就像是坐在桌旁炫耀一样。

sentences.en: Yeah, showing off.
sentences.zh: 对，炫耀。

sentences.en: Of course, of course.
sentences.zh: 当然，当然。

sentences.en: Hey, what's the latest thing?
sentences.zh: 嘿，最新有什么？

sentences.en: Have you seen this that you can really do that kind of thing?
sentences.zh: 你见过这个吗，你真的能做到那种程度吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, we were nerds.
sentences.zh: 对，我们都是书呆子。

sentences.en: To be honest, we were nerds.
sentences.zh: 说实话，我们就是书呆子。

sentences.en: But they were nerds that knew how to party.
sentences.zh: 但他们是懂得如何派对的书呆子。

sentences.en: So we were drunk, yeah.
sentences.zh: 所以我们喝醉了，是的。

sentences.en: But the party wasn't really the thing.
sentences.zh: 但派对其实并不是重点。

sentences.en: The whole inspiration and lightning came the day after, next morning.
sentences.zh: 真正的灵感和灵光乍现是在第二天，也就是第二天早晨。

sentences.en: When you're in this kind of very, a bit fragile mood.
sentences.zh: 当你处于这种非常脆弱、有点崩溃的心情时。

sentences.en: In other words, Vesku woke up hungover.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，韦斯库醒来时宿醉了。

sentences.en: And you have to find a way to survive the coming day.
sentences.zh: 你必须想办法熬过接下来的一天。

sentences.en: Gloomy morning.
sentences.zh: 阴沉的早晨。

sentences.en: Windy.
sentences.zh: 有风。

sentences.en: Really windy morning.
sentences.zh: 风真的很大的早晨。

sentences.en: And I was walking from my home to the office.
sentences.zh: 我正从家里步行去办公室。

sentences.en: That's about two miles.
sentences.zh: 大约有两英里远。

sentences.en: It was cold and dark and my phone rang.
sentences.zh: 又冷又黑，我的手机响了。

sentences.en: And it was this Nokia 2.
sentences.zh: 是个诺基亚2。

sentences.en: Didi-di-di-di-di-di-di-di-di-di-di-di-di-di-di.
sentences.zh: 滴滴滴滴滴滴滴滴滴滴滴滴滴滴滴。

sentences.en: Vesku was just barely hanging on.
sentences.zh: 韦斯库当时已经快要撑不住了。

sentences.en: The last thing he needed was this annoying sound going off.
sentences.zh: 他最不需要的就是这个烦人的声音响个不停。

sentences.en: And then I decided, now is enough.
sentences.zh: 然后我决定，够了。

sentences.en: We gotta do something with this thing.
sentences.zh: 我们得拿这东西做点什么。

sentences.en: If Vesku's phone was going to ring, it was going to make the sounds he wanted, on his terMs.
sentences.zh: 如果韦斯库的手机要响，它就得按他的意愿、发出他想要的音乐。

sentences.en: I really wanted to hear Van Halen's jump.
sentences.zh: 我真的很想听到范·海伦的《跃》。

sentences.en: Or at least a Nokia cell phone version of Van Halen's jump.
sentences.zh: 或者至少是诺基亚手机版的范·海伦的《跃》。

sentences.en: It's a power song.
sentences.zh: 这是一首充满力量的歌。

sentences.en: It would have been so, so much better to hear the...
sentences.zh: 能听到……那感觉该有多好啊。

sentences.en: All that stuff.
sentences.zh: 所有那些东西。

sentences.en: It's a positive song for me.
sentences.zh: 对我和说这是一首积极向上的歌。

sentences.en: And Eddie Van Halen, he's a legend with his guitar.
sentences.zh: 埃迪·范·海伦，他是个弹吉他的传奇人物。

sentences.en: So Vesku got to work trying to get Eddie Van Halen into his cell phone.
sentences.zh: 于是韦斯库开始着手把埃迪·范·海伦弄进他的手机里。

sentences.en: The Nokia phones Vesku and its friends were using had this early text messaging function called smart messaging
sentences.zh: 韦斯库和他的朋友们使用的诺基亚手机带有一种早期短信功能叫智能信息，

sentences.en: that let Nokia users send messages to each other.
sentences.zh: 它允许诺基亚用户互相发送信息。

sentences.en: Vesku and his squad realized that they could compose ringtones in a program Vesku created called Harmonium
sentences.zh: 韦斯库和他的小队意识到，他们可以在韦斯库创建的一个名为Harmonium的程序中创作铃声，

sentences.en: and then use that smart messaging platform to transfer bits of song as code to a cell phone.
sentences.zh: 然后使用该智能信息平台将歌曲片段作为代码传输到手机上。

sentences.en: Let's put it this way, that the guys that I was working with, they were capable of doing all kind of cracking and hacking.
sentences.zh: 这么说吧，跟我一起工作的那些家伙，他们能够搞定各种破解和黑客技术。

sentences.en: Vesku started fooling around on Harmonium and came up with the stripped-down monophonic version of his favorite pump-up jam.
sentences.zh: 韦斯库开始在Harmonium上瞎琢磨，并创作出了他最喜欢的打气金曲的精简单音版本。

sentences.en: Vesku loaded the ringtone on his phone and he really wanted someone to give him a call when he was out in public.
sentences.zh: 韦斯库把铃声加载到手机上，他真的很想在公共场合时有人给他打电话。

sentences.en: And his big moment came on the way to a meeting on a packed rush hour train.
sentences.zh: 他的高光时刻出现在去开会的路上，在一辆挤满人的早高峰列车上。

sentences.en: Someone called his phone and Jump screamed from his pocket.
sentences.zh: 有人打他的电话，《跃》从他的口袋里尖叫出来。

sentences.en: Everyone in the train was staring at him and he loved it.
sentences.zh: 车厢里的每个人都盯着他看，他喜欢这种感觉。

sentences.en: The custom ringtone was born.
sentences.zh: 定制铃声诞生了。

sentences.en: But not everyone was going to be able to hack their flip phone the way that Vesku and his friends did.
sentences.zh: 但并不是所有人都能像韦斯库和他的朋友那样去破解他们的翻盖手机。

sentences.en: So he decided that he wanted to find a way to make custom ringtones easily accessible to the masses.
sentences.zh: 于是他决定寻找一种方法，让大众也能轻松获得定制铃声。

sentences.en: Now we know that we can do that and we have to spread the gospel.
sentences.zh: 现在我们知道我们可以做到这一点，我们必须传播这个理念。

sentences.en: We have to provide this opportunity to everyone and provide some kind of a service or application for anybody to be able to customize their ringtone.
sentences.zh: 我们必须为每个人提供这个机会，并提供某种服务或应用程序，让任何人都能定制他们的铃声。

sentences.en: Vesku wanted everyone to be able to hear exactly the melody they wanted so they could show off their phones and be the coolest nerd at the nerd party.
sentences.zh: 韦斯库希望每个人都能听到他们想要的旋律，这样他们就可以炫耀自己的手机，成为书呆子派对中最酷的书呆子。

sentences.en: And so he started pitching telephone companies on the idea of an application that would allow people to create, share, and download custom ringtones.
sentences.zh: 于是他开始向电信公司推销这样一款应用程序的想法：它能让人们创作、分享和下载定制铃声。

sentences.en: And then one day, this Finnish wireless provider called Radiolinja said yes.
sentences.zh: 直到有一天，一家名为Radiolinja的芬兰无线运营商答应了。

sentences.en: They took Vesku's idea and scaled it up.
sentences.zh: 他们采用了韦斯库的想法并将其规模化。

sentences.en: The whole thing, the phenomenon, started to spread.
sentences.zh: 整件事情，这个现象，开始传播开来。

sentences.en: It's like a meme.
sentences.zh: 就像一个梗一样。

sentences.en: You are in a bus or a train, commuting or whatever, and you hear a custom ringtone.
sentences.zh: 你在公交车或火车上，在通勤或做别的什么，然后你听到一个定制铃声。

sentences.en: And your first idea is that that's not the Nokia ringtone.
sentences.zh: 你的第一个念头是那不是诺基亚的默认铃声。

sentences.en: Where the guy got it?
sentences.zh: 这家伙从哪弄来的？

sentences.en: Vesku's software allowed anyone with time on their hands to make their own musical ringtone creations.
sentences.zh: 韦斯库的软件让任何有空闲时间的人都能创作自己的音乐铃声。

sentences.en: But most people didn't have time on their hands.
sentences.zh: 但大多数人并没有那么多空闲时间。

sentences.en: I would say that 99.9% of the people just want to have the ringtone in their phone.
sentences.zh: 我想说99.9%的人只是想让铃声直接在手机里。

sentences.en: Which meant they needed a massive library of everyone's favorite songs in ringtone form.
sentences.zh: 这意味着他们需要一个庞大的资料库，里面存有每个人最喜欢的歌曲的铃声版。

sentences.en: And to build that library, they needed ringtone composers.
sentences.zh: 为了建立这个资料库，他们需要铃声编曲师。

sentences.en: Composers like Mike Levine.
sentences.zh: 像迈克·莱文这样的编曲师。

sentences.en: One thing that would take a lot of my time during the day was to think,
sentences.zh: 我白天要花很多时间去思考的一件事就是，

sentences.en: how do I boil down a song with a lot of voices down to just one simple melody line?
sentences.zh: 我该如何把一首有很多声部的歌浓缩成一个简单的旋律线条？

sentences.en: Mike worked for a ringtone company called Zingy while he was studying technology at NYU.
sentences.zh: 迈克在纽约大学学习科技专业时，曾为一家名为Zingy的铃声公司工作。

sentences.en: He found the job listing on CraigsliSt.
sentences.zh: 他在Craigslist上找到了这个工作招聘信息。

sentences.en: And he says that being a ringtone composer was kind of like being a translator.
sentences.zh: 他说当铃声编曲师有点像当翻译。

sentences.en: Each tune was a little puzzle.
sentences.zh: 每一首曲子都是一个小谜题。

sentences.en: This is something you have to think of like if you're doing a song Hey Ya by OutKaSt.
sentences.zh: 这就像你在处理一首歌，比如OutKast的《Hey Ya》。

sentences.en: You'd have to think of just that melody line.
sentences.zh: 你必须只提取出那段旋律。

sentences.en: And do it in such a way where it would still communicate, you know, what the song was to folks.
sentences.zh: 并用一种依然能让大家听出那是哪首歌的方式把它做出来。

sentences.en: By 2004, Zingy was one of the biggest ringtone producers in the world.
sentences.zh: 到2004年，Zingy已成为全球最大的铃声制作商之一。

sentences.en: The company says it was selling 2.5 million ringtones a month.
sentences.zh: 该公司表示，它每个月能售出250万个铃声。

sentences.en: And these were basic monophonic ringtones.
sentences.zh: 这些都是基础的单音铃声。

sentences.en: Simple bleeps and bloops.
sentences.zh: 简单的哔哔声和嘟嘟声。

sentences.en: Like this.
sentences.zh: 就像这样。

sentences.en: Getting cell phones around the world to play a super stripped down version of Final Countdown might not seem that impressive today.
sentences.zh: 让全世界的手机播放超级简化版的《最后一秒》，在今天看来可能没那么让人惊叹。

sentences.en: But at the time, it required a huge amount of work.
sentences.zh: 但在当时，这需要大量的工作。

sentences.en: Especially because each different brand of phone required its own custom sound file.
sentences.zh: 尤其是因为每个不同品牌的手机都需要自己定制的音频文件。

sentences.en: And so Mike and the composer Zedzingy had to program different ringtones for each phone manufacturer.
sentences.zh: 因此，迈克和作曲家泽德济尼不得不为每个手机制造商编写不同的铃声。

sentences.en: And so we would have to create the same monophonic ringtone like 20 different times.
sentences.zh: 所以我们得把同一个单音铃声制作大概20个不同的版本。

sentences.en: It was enormously tedious.
sentences.zh: 这实在是太枯燥了。

sentences.en: We had a whole bank of phones that we would use for testing these two.
sentences.zh: 我们有一整排手机，用来测试这两种手机。

sentences.en: And all these were like bricks.
sentences.zh: 而且这些手机都像砖头一样重。

sentences.en: Like huge phones.
sentences.zh: 就像巨大的手机。

sentences.en: But phones eventually got smaller and cheaper.
sentences.zh: 但手机最终变得更小、更便宜了。

sentences.en: And the business model began to change.
sentences.zh: 商业模式也开始发生变化。

sentences.en: Phone companies started giving away phones for very little money.
sentences.zh: 手机公司开始以极低的价格赠送手机。

sentences.en: With the idea that they would make their profits on the contract and other services like ringtones.
sentences.zh: 他们的想法是，他们将通过合约以及铃声等其他服务来获利。

sentences.en: And that created a demand for better, more musically complex ringtones.
sentences.zh: 这催生了对更好、音乐性更复杂的铃声的需求。

sentences.en: Polyphonic ringtones started entering the market.
sentences.zh: 和弦铃声开始进入市场。

sentences.en: And it was like, hallelujah, we can create four different channels of audio.
sentences.zh: 当时的感觉简直是，太棒了，我们可以创作四个不同的音频通道了。

sentences.en: Amazing.
sentences.zh: 太神奇了。

sentences.en: And I was so just overjoyed to be able to create like actual kick drums and snare druMs.
sentences.zh: 能够创作出真正的底鼓和小军鼓，我当时真是高兴极了。

sentences.en: Polyphonic ringtones meant that instead of one note at a time, you could get four notes at one time.
sentences.zh: 和弦铃声意味着，过去一次只能发一个音，现在你可以同时发出四个音了。

sentences.en: And so the classic Nokia ringtone came alive in a blaze of polyphonic glory.
sentences.zh: 于是，经典的诺基亚铃声在和弦铃声的辉煌中焕发了生机。

sentences.en: With polyphonic ringtones, composers were able to move beyond code.
sentences.zh: 有了和弦铃声，作曲家们得以超越代码的限制。

sentences.en: And they didn't have to completely reprogram the song for every phone manufacturer.
sentences.zh: 他们不必为每个手机制造商完全重新编写歌曲。

sentences.en: Now they can actually start using keyboards to map out their creations.
sentences.zh: 现在他们真的可以开始使用键盘来规划他们的创作了。

sentences.en: If you're doing a rock and roll track, you have to decide how many of those four tracks you're going to give to the druMs.
sentences.zh: 如果你在制作一首摇滚乐，你必须决定将这四个音轨中的多少个分配给鼓。

sentences.en: How many are you going to give to, let's say, a guitar or a bass line.
sentences.zh: 你要把多少个分配给，比方说，吉他或贝斯。

sentences.en: And how many are you going to give to the voice.
sentences.zh: 又要分配多少个给主唱。

sentences.en: This was the golden age of the ringtone.
sentences.zh: 这是铃声的黄金时代。

sentences.en: When composers like Mike Levine were cranking out their greatest works of ringtone art.
sentences.zh: 当时像迈克·莱文这样的作曲家正在源源不断地创作出他们最伟大的铃声艺术作品。

sentences.en: Mike was actually responsible for one of my favorite ringtones ever.
sentences.zh: 迈克实际上创作了我最喜欢的铃声之一。

sentences.en: Back in high school, I was a huge Kanye West fan.
sentences.zh: 高中时，我是坎耶·韦斯特的超级粉丝。

sentences.en: I grew up outside of Chicago, around the time that Kanye and ringtones were both blowing up.
sentences.zh: 我在芝加哥郊外长大，正赶上坎耶和铃声双双爆红的时期。

sentences.en: Kanye's second album, Late Registration, had recently been released.
sentences.zh: 坎耶的第二张专辑《Late Registration》最近刚刚发行。

sentences.en: Aside from the big singles like Gold Digger and Heard Him Say,
sentences.zh: 除了《Gold Digger》和《Heard Him Say》这样的大热单曲，

sentences.en: my absolute favorite song was a small cut towards the end of the album.
sentences.zh: 我绝对最喜欢的是专辑末尾的一首小众歌曲。

sentences.en: Track number 17.
sentences.zh: 第17首。

sentences.en: It's a slow-moving track with a dense orchestral build.
sentences.zh: 这是一首节奏缓慢、管弦乐编曲层层递进的歌曲。

sentences.en: Almost like the falling action of the album.
sentences.zh: 几乎就像专辑的回落部分。

sentences.en: The song is called Celebration.
sentences.zh: 这首歌叫《Celebration》。

sentences.en: I love the production of this track.
sentences.zh: 我非常喜欢这首歌的制作。

sentences.en: I felt like I was on screen starring in a movie of my life whenever I listened to it.
sentences.zh: 每当我听它的时候，我都觉得自己在银幕上主演着自己的人生电影。

sentences.en: It gave me confidence.
sentences.zh: 它给了我自信。

sentences.en: Kanye's Celebration was like the perfect musical representation of myself.
sentences.zh: 坎耶的《Celebration》就像是我个人的完美音乐写照。

sentences.en: Which made it the perfect ringtone.
sentences.zh: 这使它成为了完美的铃声。

sentences.en: You know what time it is.
sentences.zh: 你知道现在是什么时间。

sentences.en: It's a celebration, bitches.
sentences.zh: 这是个庆祝活动，婊子们。

sentences.en: Sorry, I couldn't not end that.
sentences.zh: 抱歉，我忍不住要用这个结尾。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: No, I'm highly certain that your version was probably the one I downloaded.
sentences.zh: 不，我很确定你下载的可能就是我的版本。

sentences.en: Stop it.
sentences.zh: 别这样。

sentences.en: No way.
sentences.zh: 不会吧。

sentences.en: Yeah, I'm pretty sure your work was the soundtrack of my late high school years.
sentences.zh: 是的，我很确信你的作品就是我高中晚期的背景音乐。

sentences.en: This is amazing, James.
sentences.zh: 这太神奇了，詹姆斯。

sentences.en: Like, that's probably the coolest thing I can imagine.
sentences.zh: 这可能是我能想象到的最酷的事情了。

sentences.en: Oh my God, I love it.
sentences.zh: 哦天哪，我太喜欢了。

sentences.en: I love it.
sentences.zh: 我太喜欢了。

sentences.en: Oh, fan of my work here.
sentences.zh: 哦，原来这里有我的作品的粉丝。

sentences.en: In a short period of time, ringtones became a booming business.
sentences.zh: 在很短的时间内，铃声变成了一项蓬勃发展的业务。

sentences.en: But using all these popular songs meant companies like Zingy needed to get the rights to them.
sentences.zh: 但使用所有这些流行歌曲意味着像Zingy这样的公司需要获得它们的版权。

sentences.en: So, a lot of my recollection of my time there was working in a very fast pace.
sentences.zh: 所以，我对那段时光的很多回忆都是在快节奏的工作中度过的。

sentences.en: Like, we need to be the first to get this out.
sentences.zh: 比如，我们需要第一个把这个推向市场。

sentences.en: Let's do it.
sentences.zh: 我们干吧。

sentences.en: Let's figure out who has the rights.
sentences.zh: 弄清楚谁拥有版权。

sentences.en: Let's go get them.
sentences.zh: 我们去把版权拿下。

sentences.en: That's Stacey Ibrahach.
sentences.zh: 那是斯黛西·易卜拉罕。

sentences.en: She handled the licensing over at Zingy.
sentences.zh: 她在Zingy负责版权许可工作。

sentences.en: There was a content team that identified all the hot songs that were coming out.
sentences.zh: 有一个内容团队负责挑选所有即将问世的热门歌曲。

sentences.en: They gave folks like Stacey a heads up.
sentences.zh: 他们会给像斯黛西这样的人提前打招呼。

sentences.en: And then she went into action.
sentences.zh: 然后她就开始行动了。

sentences.en: Say, hey, this new song is going to drop by X artiSt.
sentences.zh: 说，嘿，某某艺人的这首新歌要发布了。

sentences.en: And we need to make sure that we have the ringtone rights the day the song drops.
sentences.zh: 我们需要确保在歌曲发布的当天就拥有铃声版权。

sentences.en: And so, oftentimes, our job was feverishly trying within the space of hours to figure out which publishers and labels owned rights to certain songs.
sentences.zh: 所以通常情况下，我们的工作就是在几个小时内拼命摸索，弄清楚哪些出版商和唱片公司拥有某些歌曲的版权。

sentences.en: How did we get those rights?
sentences.zh: 我们是怎么获得这些版权的？

sentences.en: All of these forces, the licensing, tech, and the business, came together to usher in the final, fully evolved form of the ringtone.
sentences.zh: 所有这些力量——版权许可、技术和商业——汇聚在一起，迎来了铃声的最终完全进化形态。

sentences.en: The real tone.
sentences.zh: 真实铃声。

sentences.en: Real tones were basically just snippets of the song, cut down to size.
sentences.zh: 真实铃声基本上就是歌曲的片段，经过裁剪缩短。

sentences.en: Like Uncle Scooter's ringtone.
sentences.zh: 就像韦斯库叔叔的铃声一样。

sentences.en: It was just that Maxwell song.
sentences.zh: 那只是麦克斯韦的歌。

sentences.en: It was the closest thing to listening to music on our phones in the mid-2000s.
sentences.zh: 那是2000年代中期在手机上听音乐的最接近的体验。

sentences.en: And as cool as it was to finally hear music on your phone in high fidelity, for composers like Mike, it was hard not to see the rise of the real tone as something of a loss.
sentences.zh: 尽管终于能在手机上听到高保真的音乐很酷，但对于像迈克这样的作曲家来说，很难不把真实铃声的崛起视为什么损失。

sentences.en: Once we got the rights to the actual songs and once the technology got savvy enough, we became much more editors at that point than anything else.
sentences.zh: 一旦我们获得了实际歌曲的版权，一旦技术足够成熟，我们在那个时候就更像是编辑，而不是别的什么了。

sentences.en: We missed getting to actually get into the nitty-gritty and create the audio ourselves.
sentences.zh: 我们怀念能够真正深入细节并自己创作音频的日子。

sentences.en: And that bleepy, bloopy ringtone aesthetic was gone forever.
sentences.zh: 那种哔哔啵啵的铃声美学永远消失了。

sentences.en: Ringtones were just music now.
sentences.zh: 铃声现在就是音乐本身。

sentences.en: Even the classic Nokia ringtone.
sentences.zh: 甚至是经典的诺基亚铃声。

sentences.en: And once you could put any sound on a phone, why limit yourself to music?
sentences.zh: 既然你可以在手机上播放任何声音，为什么还要把自己局限在音乐上呢？

sentences.en: Our largest market were like younger, mostly boys, based on a lot of like polling data that we had.
sentences.zh: 根据我们掌握的大量民意调查数据，我们最大的市场是年轻人，主要是男孩。

sentences.en: And so I created ringtones called Burping Cow, Farting Donkey.
sentences.zh: 所以我创作了名为《打嗝的牛》、《放屁的驴》的铃声。

sentences.en: That's some classy stuff.
sentences.zh: 这可真高级。

sentences.en: I used to bring home just myself, like 3-4k a month, just selling this stuff, you know?
sentences.zh: 我以前光靠卖这些东西，每个月就能净赚3到4千美元，你知道吗？

sentences.en: I joke around that it's the opposite of Edison's formula.
sentences.zh: 我开玩笑说这和爱迪生的公式相反。

sentences.en: This is like 99% inspiration, 1% perspiration.
sentences.zh: 这就像是99%的灵感，1%的汗水。

sentences.en: Because these take like a matter of minutes to create, you know?
sentences.zh: 因为这些制作只需要几分钟，你知道吗？

sentences.en: I would just find like samples of a donkey and like farting noises.
sentences.zh: 我只需要找一些驴子的采样和放屁的声音。

sentences.en: It's about as dumb as it sounds.
sentences.zh: 听起来有多蠢，做出来就有多蠢。

sentences.en: With millions of cell phone users buying real-tone pop songs and donkey farts, ringtones became a cash cow.
sentences.zh: 随着数百万手机用户购买真实铃声流行歌曲和驴屁声，铃声成了一只会下金蛋的母鸡。

sentences.en: And not just for the cell phone companies.
sentences.zh: 而且不仅仅是对手机公司而言。

sentences.en: Also for the music industry, which was struggling in the early 2000s.
sentences.zh: 对在2000年代初苦苦挣扎的音乐产业来说也是如此。

sentences.en: In the early 2000s was the rise of file sharing, both of, you know, legal and illegal kinds.
sentences.zh: 2000年代初是文件共享兴起的时期，包括合法的和非法的。

sentences.en: And this helped to, you know, cause a major decrease in music recording industry revenue.
sentences.zh: 这导致了音乐唱片行业收入的大幅下降。

sentences.en: And so the ringtone was seen as a way of kind of making up for that.
sentences.zh: 因此，铃声被视为弥补这一损失的一种方式。

sentences.en: This is Samant Gopentath.
sentences.zh: 这位是萨曼·戈彭塔斯。

sentences.en: He's a professor of music theory and he wrote a whole book about the ringtone industry.
sentences.zh: 他是一位音乐理论教授，写了一整本关于铃声产业的书。

sentences.en: Gopentath says that realtones became an increasingly valuable piece of intellectual property for music publishing companies.
sentences.zh: 戈彭塔斯表示，对于音乐出版公司来说，真实铃声正成为一种价值不断增长的知识产权。

sentences.en: Who owns a song is the publishing company.
sentences.zh: 拥有歌曲所有权的是出版公司。

sentences.en: And so it's the publishing company that gives you permission to, you know, kind of essentially use the material of the song.
sentences.zh: 所以是出版公司允许你，你知道的，基本上使用这首歌的素材。

sentences.en: The realtones, which were actual snippets of the songs, allowed the music industry to have more control.
sentences.zh: 真实铃声也就是歌曲的实际片段，让音乐产业拥有了更多的控制权。

sentences.en: So they were able to charge a higher price and get a bigger cut.
sentences.zh: 因此他们能够收取更高的价格并获得更大的分成。

sentences.en: The realtone may have helped the music companies, but it ended up being the beginning of the end for the ringtone industry.
sentences.zh: 真实铃声可能帮助了音乐公司，但它最终成为了铃声产业回光返照的开始。

sentences.en: The custom ringtone met its demise, according to Samant, for a few reasons.
sentences.zh: 萨曼认为，个性化铃声走向消亡有几个原因。

sentences.en: As smartphones improved, people just started using their own MP3s as ringtones.
sentences.zh: 随着智能手机的改进，人们开始直接使用自己的MP3作为铃声。

sentences.en: It became much easier to just copy them and get them on your phone.
sentences.zh: 复制并通过手机播放变得容易多了。

sentences.en: Also, scammers got into the ringtone business and started scaring off the customers.
sentences.zh: 此外，骗子也进入了铃声行业，开始把客户吓跑。

sentences.en: But the biggest reason was that it just became too much.
sentences.zh: 但最大的原因是它实在太过吵闹了。

sentences.en: If everyone had their own cell phone with their own little cute ringtone, public spaces got really noisy.
sentences.zh: 如果每个人都有自己的手机，播放着自己可爱的小铃声，公共场所就会变得非常嘈杂。

sentences.en: And so everyone just started putting their phones on vibrate.
sentences.zh: 于是大家开始把手机调成振动模式。

sentences.en: There is a kind of social policing that's really has also taken place to reduce sort of public phone communication practices.
sentences.zh: 某种社会规范的约束也确实在发生，以减少公共场所的手机通话行为。

sentences.en: And the ringtones, you know, decline is a part of that.
sentences.zh: 而铃声的衰落正是其中的一部分。

sentences.en: Phones became more functional.
sentences.zh: 手机变得更加实用。

sentences.en: Texting got better and faster and more convenient.
sentences.zh: 短信变得更好、更快、更方便。

sentences.en: Our phones became full-on pocket computers and entertainment devices with headphones.
sentences.zh: 我们的手机变成了成熟的口袋电脑和带有耳机的娱乐设备。

sentences.en: People are using their phones as part of creating kind of private auditory bubbles for themselves.
sentences.zh: 人们正在利用手机为自己创造某种私密的听觉气泡。

sentences.en: And this spelled the N for ringtone companies like Zingy and ringtone makers like Mike.
sentences.zh: 这敲响了像Zingy这样的铃声公司和像迈克这样的铃声制作人的丧钟。

sentences.en: I'll be honest, by like mid-07, it became an almost daily expectation.
sentences.zh: 说实话，到07年中期，这几乎成了每天都会有的预期。

sentences.en: Be like, we knew, you know, this axe was going to fall any time.
sentences.zh: 就像是，我们知道，这把达摩克利斯之剑随时都会落下。

sentences.en: We just didn't know when it was going to come.
sentences.zh: 我们只是不知道它什么时候会来。

sentences.en: And everybody was just thinking, we're all making good money here.
sentences.zh: 每个人都在想，我们在这里都赚到了好钱。

sentences.en: Let's just enjoy it while it lasts.
sentences.zh: 趁它还在，好好享受吧。

sentences.en: Unfortunately for Mike, the axe fell just as swiftly as he feared.
sentences.zh: 不幸的是，对于迈克来说，这把剑落下的速度和他担心的一样快。

sentences.en: I believe it was September or October of 07, it happened.
sentences.zh: 我记得那是07年的9月或10月发生的。

sentences.en: And our new CEO at that time came around and basically fired our whole content group.
sentences.zh: 当时我们的新CEO来了，基本上把我们的整个内容团队都解雇了。

sentences.en: It was about 35 to 40 people let go at once.
sentences.zh: 当时有大约35到40人同时被解雇。

sentences.en: The day the music died.
sentences.zh: 音乐死去的日子。

sentences.en: Yeah, it was not a happy day.
sentences.zh: 是的，那不是开心的一天。

sentences.en: Over a decade later, our phones are touchscreened mini computers that never leave our sides.
sentences.zh: 十多年后的今天，我们的手机变成了从不离身的触屏迷你电脑。

sentences.en: They are our music players, our televisions, our portal to the world.
sentences.zh: 它们是我们的音乐播放器、我们的电视，是我们通往世界的门户。

sentences.en: And in a way, it all kind of started with Vescu and his need to have Van Halen on his flip phone.
sentences.zh: 从某种意义上说，这一切都始于韦斯库和他想要在翻盖手机上播放范·海伦音乐的需求。

sentences.en: We proved that there is such thing as a mobile entertainment.
sentences.zh: 我们证明了移动娱乐是真实存在的。

sentences.en: There's a business there and it will change the old world.
sentences.zh: 那里有商机，它将改变旧世界。

sentences.en: Vescu remembers his little place in history every time his phone rings.
sentences.zh: 每当手机响起，韦斯库都会想起他在历史上的那一小席之地。

sentences.en: Let me see.
sentences.zh: 让我看看。

sentences.en: It's switched my phone on here.
sentences.zh: 我的手机在这里开机了。

sentences.en: It's not a polyphonic ringtone.
sentences.zh: 这不是一个和弦铃声。

sentences.en: It's just an MP3 file that plays when Vescu gets a call.
sentences.zh: 这只是韦斯库接到电话时播放的一个MP3文件。

sentences.en: But it's still something he holds on to as a form of self-expression.
sentences.zh: 但它仍然是他作为自我表达的一种形式而坚持保留的东西。

sentences.en: I think it's been there at least 15 years.
sentences.zh: 我想它至少在那里待了15年了。

sentences.en: I'm a kite surfer myself.
sentences.zh: 我自己是个风筝冲浪者。

sentences.en: So for me, surfing USA is also a statement that I'm a surfer.
sentences.zh: 所以对我和来说，《冲浪美国》也是一个声明，表明我是一个冲浪者。

sentences.en: And Vescu isn't the only one still using custom rings.
sentences.zh: 韦斯库并不是唯一一个还在使用自定义铃声的人。

sentences.en: Mike, the former ringtone maker, is now a student of musicology at the University of North Carolina.
sentences.zh: 前铃声制作人迈克现在是北卡罗来纳大学的音乐学专业学生。

sentences.en: And his ringtone screams student of musicology who still thinks about ringtones.
sentences.zh: 而他的铃声大声宣告着他是一个依然在思考铃声的音乐学学生。

sentences.en: I have been using Radiohead's Idiotech, actually, for a while, which I think makes a really good ringtone.
sentences.zh: 其实我用电台司令（Radiohead）的 Idiotech 已经有一段时间了，我觉得它当手机铃声真的很好听。

sentences.en: And don't forget about my uncle Scooter.
sentences.zh: 别忘了我叔叔斯库特（Scooter）。

sentences.en: His ringtone, 16 years later, is still that Maxwell song.
sentences.zh: 16年过去了，他的手机铃声依然是麦克斯韦（Maxwell）的那首歌。

sentences.en: In my day, when you got something, you held on to it because it was hard to come by.
sentences.zh: 在我们那个年代，你得到什么东西都会好好珍惜，因为来之不易。

sentences.en: So when you got something, you learned to take care of it and treasure that.
sentences.zh: 所以当你拥有了某样东西，你就会学会爱护它、珍视它。

sentences.en: And I guess it carried over into my adulthood, especially with something that you like.
sentences.zh: 我想这种习惯也延续到了我的成年生活中，尤其是对你喜欢的东西。

sentences.en: I love this ringtone and I held on to it for dear life.
sentences.zh: 我太喜欢这个铃声了，我死死抓着它不放。

sentences.en: And I'll probably have this ringtone until I die.
sentences.zh: 我大概到死都会用这个铃声吧。

sentences.en: I may not have a Maxwell ringtone on my deathbed, but after reporting this story, I decided I'm not going to keep my phone on silent anymore.
sentences.zh: 我临终前可能不会用麦克斯韦的铃声，但在报道了这个故事之后，我决定以后再也不把手机调成静音了。

sentences.en: I'm using ringtones again, and I think a lot about which ringtone to use on a given day.
sentences.zh: 我又开始用铃声了，而且我经常琢磨某一天该用哪首铃声。

sentences.en: My default is one of my favorite Yeah Yeah Yeah song.
sentences.zh: 我的默认铃声是我最喜欢的“野草莓”（Yeah Yeah Yeahs）乐队的一首歌。

sentences.en: One that represented a pivotal moment of my life, and it brings me joy every time a telemarketer calls.
sentences.zh: 这首歌代表了我人生的一个关键时刻，每次有推销电话打来时，它都会给我带来快乐。

sentences.en: If I travel, I'll switch it up to match wherever I'm going.
sentences.zh: 如果我外出旅行，我会把铃声换成与目的地相配的音乐。

sentences.en: Kind of like how someone reads a book about the place that they're visiting.
sentences.zh: 有点像人们会阅读关于他们正在访问的地方的书籍那样。

sentences.en: If I'm in the D.C.
sentences.zh: 如果我在华盛顿特区

sentences.en: area, I may switch up my ringtone to a Goldblink song.
sentences.zh: 地区，我可能会把铃声换成 Goldblink 的歌。

sentences.en: The week that NPR's Morning Edition changed their theme song, R.I.P., I made my ringtone the original theme.
sentences.zh: 就在 NPR 的《早间新闻》（Morning Edition）更换主题曲的那周，安息吧，我把原版主题曲设成了我的铃声。

sentences.en: I think of ringtones kind of like enamel pins or tote bags or baseball caps.
sentences.zh: 我觉得手机铃声有点像搪瓷徽章、托特包或者棒球帽。

sentences.en: They're a simple way for me to show off my tastes in an increasingly templatized world.
sentences.zh: 在这个日益格式化的世界里，它们是我展示自己品味的一种简单方式。

sentences.en: So, a modest suggestion here for the next time you go out in public.
sentences.zh: 所以，下次你公开露面时，我有一个小小的建议。

sentences.en: Take your phone off vibrate.
sentences.zh: 把你的手机取消震动。

sentences.en: Load up your favorite song, something that says something about you.
sentences.zh: 放上你最喜欢的歌，一首能代表你个性的歌。

sentences.en: Turn the volume up and wait for a robot scammer to call.
sentences.zh: 把音量调大，等着推销机器人的电话打进来。

sentences.zh: 完全是，完全是。

sentences.en: Saying it out loud, giving ourselves a little performance.
sentences.zh: 大声说出来，自己给自己演上一出。

sentences.en: And then until we've really, really just have the perfect comeback and we can pat ourselves on the back.
sentences.zh: 直到我们真的、真的想出了完美的回击，然后可以拍拍自己的背以示鼓励。

sentences.en: And, you know, on some level when we do this, we can poke fun at it and say that it's kind of petty of us and kind of silly and we're just stroking our fragile egos.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，某种程度上当我们这么做时，我们也可以拿它开玩笑，说我们这有点小肚鸡肠，有点傻里傻气，我们只是在抚慰自己脆弱的自尊心。

sentences.en: But I actually think this idea of Treppenwitz, this idea of, like, coming up with the comeback later, actually does serve a kind of healthy psychological purpose,
sentences.zh: 但我其实觉得，“楼梯灵感”这个概念——也就是事后才想出漂亮回击的这种想法——其实确实发挥了一种健康的心理作用，

sentences.en: which is it allows you to get over the thing, right?
sentences.zh: 那就是它能让你放下这件事，对吧？

sentences.en: It allows you to kind of put it behind you and put it in its place and walk away kind of with your ego healthily intact.
sentences.zh: 它能让你把这件事抛在脑后，把它摆在正确的位置，然后安然无恙、毫发无损地走开。

sentences.en: Right, right.
sentences.zh: 对的，对的。

sentences.en: And I think one of the reasons I've never forgotten this scene and why every time I think about it and I think about it way too often,
sentences.zh: 而且我觉得我之所以永远忘不了这一幕，为什么每次我想起它时——而且我想它的频率实在太高了——

sentences.en: it just continues to irk me in this way that is disproportionate to its actual importance is because I've never thought of the perfect comeback.
sentences.zh: 它总是继续以一种与其实际重要性不成比例的方式烦扰着我，就是因为我从来没想出过那个完美的回击。

sentences.en: It's such a complicated.
sentences.zh: 这真的是一个复杂的……

sentences.en: I totally know what you mean.
sentences.zh: 我完全明白你的意思。

sentences.en: It's such a complicated situation with so many layers that would require so much explanation to actually, like,
sentences.zh: 这是一个如此复杂、包含多层面的情况，需要大量的解释才能真正让对方……

sentences.en: get the person up to speed to explain to her the context and the exposition and everything such that she would understand the situation such that I would be able to then deliver the comeback.
sentences.zh: 让对方跟上节奏，向她解释来龙去脉、背景和一切，好让她能理解当时的状况，然后我才能说出那个回击。

sentences.en: It's almost, like, uncombackable.
sentences.zh: 这简直是……根本无法回击的。

sentences.en: And I just – and so it's actually – I've never been able to kind of purge it and it's haunted me to this day.
sentences.zh: 我只是——所以实际上——我从来没能把它从心里排解出去，它直到今天还纠缠着我。

sentences.en: But I will say there's something else about this incident that didn't occur to me until we started working on this story,
sentences.zh: 但我得说，关于这件事还有另一处细节，直到我们开始制作这个故事我才突然意识到，

sentences.en: which is that this was something that could have only happened at this moment in history circa 2004.
sentences.zh: 那就是这件事只可能发生在2004年前后历史上的这个特定时刻。

sentences.en: So obviously this is a real tone, right?
sentences.zh: 所以很明显，这是一种真实的音调，对吧？

sentences.en: It's a real tone.
sentences.zh: 这是一种真实的音调。

sentences.en: It's a recording of a woman's voice.
sentences.zh: 这是一段女人的录音。

sentences.en: It's not polyphonic.
sentences.zh: 它不是复调的。

sentences.en: It's not monophonic.
sentences.zh: 它也不是单音的。

sentences.en: And it's much more in the donkey's farting category of things than it is in the music category of things.
sentences.zh: 它更接近于放屁声那种东西，而不是音乐那种东西。

sentences.en: But what it is is that I'm kind of stuck at this moment where two historical forces, one being, like, an unstoppable force and the other being an immovable object,
sentences.zh: 但它是这样的：我被困在了这样一个时刻，两股历史力量——一股势不可挡，另一股不可动摇——

sentences.en: are about to collide.
sentences.zh: 即将发生碰撞。

sentences.en: And one of these forces is you definitely need your own custom ringtone.
sentences.zh: 而其中一股力量是：你绝对需要你专属的个性化铃声。

sentences.en: And the other force is everyone else's custom ringtone is really annoying and everyone just needs to turn them off.
sentences.zh: 而另一股力量则是：其他所有人的个性化铃声都太烦人了，大家真该把它们都关掉。

sentences.en: Right?
sentences.zh: 对吧？

sentences.en: Totally.
sentences.zh: 完全如此。

sentences.en: And this was happening right around this time, 2003 to 2005, right?
sentences.zh: 而这正发生在那个时期左右，2003年到2005年，对吧？

sentences.en: And I got caught in the middle, in between these two forces colliding, because with this ringtone that is addressing this very issue, it is like the ultimate meta, self-reflexive,
sentences.zh: 我被夹在中间，夹在这两股碰撞的力量之间，因为带着这个直面这个问题的铃声，它就像是终极的元叙事、自我反讽，

sentences.en: scary movie five, you know, this trend is over.
sentences.zh: 就像《惊声尖笑5》那种，你知道的，这种潮流已经结束了。

sentences.en: All we can do is point to the form itself and declare ourselves superior to it.
sentences.zh: 我们能做的就是指出这种形式本身，并宣称我们比它更高明。

sentences.en: Totally.
sentences.zh: 完全是这样。

sentences.en: Right?
sentences.zh: 对吧？

sentences.en: You know, and so basically this ringtone is saying, like, aren't ringtones annoying?
sentences.zh: 你知道，所以基本上这个铃声是在说：铃声不是很烦人吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Right?
sentences.zh: 对吧？

sentences.en: And in fact, yes, they are.
sentences.zh: 事实上，没错，确实很烦。

sentences.en: And at least in the case of this one.
sentences.zh: 至少在这个铃声的例子里是这样。

sentences.en: And so this is something that, you know, could only have happened to me in this incredibly narrow window of time.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，这只可能发生在我身上，在这个极其狭窄的时间窗口里。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: When this kind of Hegelian dialectic of ringtones and no ringtones, you know, thesis, antithesis collides and created something new in its wake.
sentences.zh: 当铃声与无铃声的这种黑格尔辩证法，也就是正题与反题发生碰撞，并在其余波中创造出新事物的时候。

sentences.en: Like, all right, that's all I got.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我能说的就这么多了。

sentences.en: So if one of the problems with this story is that you've never come up with the perfect comeback, the perfect Treppenvitz to ease your mind,
sentences.zh: 所以，如果这个故事的问题之一在于你从来没有想出那个完美的回击，那个能抚平你心头的“楼梯灵感”，

sentences.en: to assuage this sort of lingering mortification, maybe we should figure one out for you.
sentences.zh: 来缓解这种挥之不去的尴尬，也许我们应该为你想一个。

sentences.en: You know, like, I don't know if I don't think I can do it.
sentences.zh: 你知道，就像，我不知道，我觉得我可能做不到。

sentences.en: But the collective mind power of the people who listen to this show, maybe they could come up with a good comeback for you.
sentences.zh: 但听这个节目的听众们所凝聚的集体智慧，也许能为你想出一个漂亮的回击。

sentences.en: So if, like, you were in this situation and you were being browbeaten by somebody who didn't want you to answer their phone,
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你处于这种情境中，遭到某个不希望你接听他们电话的人的言语欺压，

sentences.en: even though their phone was ringing and unaccompanied in front of you, what should you say back?
sentences.zh: 尽管他们的电话就在你面前响个不停却无人接听，你应该怎么回击他们？

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: We'll see what we can do.
sentences.zh: 我们看看能做些什么。

sentences.en: That's great.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。
